hypotheses.claim: An evolved multiplicative-gate rank-power ruin score that is jointly normalized by the global depot-distance scale and adapts its rank exponent to stagnation will improve mean objective on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 versus the round-2 incumbent (16.0293), with the gains concentrated in the weakest regimes identified in the archive feedback (spatial=clustered, capacity_level=loose, size=100, depot_style=eccentric), because worst-cost removal alone over-focuses on long edges and never diversifies across routes of an eccentric-depot instance.

next_search_advice.direction: Refine the ruin priority hook `score_ruin_nodes` into a stagnation-adaptive, dimensionless multiplicative gate: rank-power of the scale-normalized removal savings with exponent p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio) that shifts from exploitation (high p, worst-cost removal) toward diversification (p→1 + randomized-deterministic geometric spread) as stagnation rises; multiply by smooth gates for route load slack (dense/loose-capacity routes first), depot proximity asymmetry (eccentric-depot instances), and within-route distance, so that clustered/loose-capacity regimes get larger ruin sets while eccentric-depot routes are ruined along their far-side arc.
